scenarios.title: An earlier route past the rival
scenarios.objective: Bring both cars home and investigate an earlier stop against a named rival.
scenarios.hint: Compare Undercut with Extend. The early stop spends a fresh set and exposes a longer final stint; a rival may cover. An opportunity is not a promised gain.

scenarios.title: Track position has a price
scenarios.objective: Compare retaining track position with paying for a fresh-tyre stop.
scenarios.hint: The fitted sets have substantial life. Review the full pit loss and likely rejoin, then retain the current plan or approve a bounded extension. No stop is compulsory.

scenarios.title: Two opportunities, one pit box
scenarios.objective: Compare a split approach for MER and MOR against running similar windows.
scenarios.hint: Read both plans before approving either. MER starts P2 and MOR P3, but their actual arrival times decide service order. An uncommitted priority cannot reorder cars already in the lane.

scenarios.title: Fresh tyres, little distance
scenarios.objective: Finish the short final-stint exercise and decide whether any stop can repay its cost.
scenarios.hint: This is a disclosed six-lap exercise from an untimed preparation grid, not an invented mid-race history. Compare stopping, extending, and no stop; every fitted set starts used.
